runners_data.name: Collateral Damage
runners_data.spotlight: By Too Darn Hot; 270,000gns foal; first foal; dam 1m AW winner; interesting newcomer who should be checked in the market.

runners_data.name: Rogue Passion
runners_data.spotlight: 90,000euros yearling; first foal; by Sioux Nation out of a 7.5f/10.3f winner; worth monitoring in the market on her debut.

runners_data.name: Wilbur
runners_data.spotlight: 160,000euros yearling by Kingman out of a 1m juvenile winner; promising 2.75l fourth of ten on last month's Newbury debut (6f, good; 16-1, not getting the best of runs); 7f should suit; improvement likely.

runners_data.name: Sou'wester
runners_data.spotlight: Has shown a degree of promise, notably when 6l fifth of seven on his Redcar debut (7f, good; 40-1); pulled hard and hung left at Beverley last time (7.5f, good to firm; 16-1) but this track should suit him better.

runners_data.name: Leave The Bag In
runners_data.comment: Encouraging start with running-on eighth at York; capable of better, especially over 7f
runners_data.spotlight: Ran green when eighth on her debut in a York novice (6f, good; 16-1) but didn't improve on that when seventh in a valuable Thirsk novice last time (7f, good; 8-1); this is easier.

races.name: Bowel Cancer Screening Programme Saves Lives Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Alpha Platoon
runners_data.note: Expensive newcomer with strong breeding but trainer Wilson is 0/3 in last 14 days, making debut impact uncertain despite pedigree appeal
runners_data.comment: Useful sprinting pedigree; attracted no interest at the sales last September; best watched
runners_data.spotlight: 55,000gns yearling; second foal of 6f AW winner (RPR 100); gelded half-brother to the 5f juvenile scorer Ain't Nobody (including Listed; 114); best watched on debut, with various question marks lingering.

runners_data.name: Two Commanders
runners_data.note: Prominent runner dropping back to 6f after weakening over 7f last time, should benefit from shorter trip tracking the expected steady pace
runners_data.comment: Half-brother to four winners at up to 1m2f; interesting newcomer; worth a market check
runners_data.spotlight: Half-brother to four winners; did as well as could be expected when a weakening third over 7f here (maiden, good to firm; 17-2) 12 days ago; dropping back to 6f should be fine, although the ground conditions are now likely to be slower; chance.

runners_data.name: Lamlash Bay
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 175-day break, needs strong pace to close into but may struggle if tempo stays conservative throughout
runners_data.comment: Lots of winners in the family but tailed off on last month's turf debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Struggled on Redcar debut (6f, good; 150-1) last November, but better at Southwell (6f; 80-1, fourth of eight, beaten 7l) the following month; eligible for a handicap mark after this comeback run.

runners_data.name: Nursia
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won cosily on Newcastle AW, carries 7lb penalty but has tactical speed to track Korbut and strike at the right moment
runners_data.comment: Well held on 2yo debut but picked up well to win over C&D in January; plenty more to come
runners_data.spotlight: Cosy Newcastle AW winner (6f novice; 13-8) in January; that form isn't easy to evaluate, the runner-up winning two Class 5 handicaps since, but the odds-on favourite (third) has yet to reappear; carries a penalty for that, and returns to turf as a gelding after a break.

runners_data.name: Sugar Bon Bon
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse switching from AW to turf for first time, finished well behind at Southwell and needs significant improvement to compete
runners_data.comment: Trainer not noted for first-time-out winners on the Flat
runners_data.spotlight: Dam was a 6f-7f winner; fifth of nine on Southwell debut (6f novice; 200-1, beaten 9l) six weeks ago; could build on that now switched to turf, but others tick more boxes at this stage of his career.

runners_data.name: Lady Gormire
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who ran well when second over course and distance 21 days ago, gets 5lb allowance and proven on the track
runners_data.comment: Failed to build on debut promise when eighth at Doncaster for Kevin Ryan; not written off
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten 12l when runner-up on debut for Kevin Ryan; joined this trainer for 12,000gns, and made a solid start when runner-up in maiden fillies' race over C&D (6-1) three weeks ago; enters calculations.

runners_data.name: Havana Oaks
runners_data.note: Lightly raced filly returning from 224-day absence, showed little in two AW starts and hard to fancy after such a long break
runners_data.spotlight: Fifth of nine on Newcastle AW debut in a 6f fillies' maiden (7-1) last October, but took a backward step at Southwell (5f; 33-1, last of five) a few weeks later; off for 224 days since so she couldn't be the pick on this turf debut; monitor only.

runners_data.name: Korbut
runners_data.note: Natural front runner who nearly stole a race at Southwell, will control the tempo but must prove she can last home when pressed late
runners_data.spotlight: Tried to pinch it at Southwell (7f fillies' novice; 33-1) on second start, but couldn't hold off the winner; ran to a similar level when fifth over that trip at Wolverhampton since; now tackles 6f for turf debut.

races.paceDynamic: Korbut is the only confirmed front runner and will take them along at her own rhythm from the start. Two Commanders, Nursia, and Lady Gormire will track her prominently, but without another genuine pace-setter, Korbut won't face early pressure. This creates a measured tempo that builds gradually, with the real action delayed until the final two furlongs when the hold-up horses like Lamlash Bay and Sugar Bon Bon try to close from off the pace. This sustainable early pace strongly favours prominent racers and front runners who can position close to Korbut and kick when she comes under pressure.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Korbut Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Korbut gets an easy lead and dictates fractions without early pressure
scenarios.body: She can kick clear turning for home before the closers get organized, while prominent trackers like Two Commanders and Lady Gormire benefit from the perfect tactical position. The measured early pace allows those handy to the speed to outkick both the lone leader and the hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners gets the perfect trip tracking Korbut's steady pace
scenarios.body: Lady Gormire or Nursia can time their challenge perfectly, passing the tiring leader while staying clear of the late closers. They get the best of both worlds - close enough to strike but not doing the donkey work up front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes too conservative and the field bunches turning for home
scenarios.body: Lamlash Bay or Sugar Bon Bon can produce a sustained finish that overwhelms horses who've been closer to the pace. The lack of early speed allows them to get into contention and finish strongest when it matters.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Alpha Platoon Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the expensive newcomer shows natural ability and gets a ground-saving trip
scenarios.body: His breeding suggests talent and the lack of pace pressure could suit a horse learning the game. Trainer Noel Wilson may have found the right spot for his debut despite his poor recent strike rate.

watchPoints.text: Korbut getting too soft a lead early - she showed she can nearly steal races when unopposed and could prove hard to peg back
Two Commanders dropping back in trip after tiring over 7f - needs to show the shorter distance suits his style better than last run suggested
Lady Gormire's fitness levels after trainer change and 21-day gap, though her course form gives her a clear edge if ready
Alpha Platoon's market support given his breeding and purchase price - any strong betting moves would signal stable confidence in debut ability
The pace development in the first two furlongs - if no horse challenges Korbut early, she could get away with murder on the front end

races.name: racingtv.com/freetrial Handicap

runners_data.name: Havin A Flyer
runners_data.note: Prominent runner perfectly placed to track uncontested leader, strips fitter after 12-day break from comeback run
runners_data.comment: Two sound runs in turf h'caps last year; on a good mark now; chance after 130-day break
runners_data.spotlight: 0-17; didn't look entirely straightforward when fourth over C&D (Powernap runner-up) 12 days ago; she could strip fitter for that comeback run though, and it's possible the added cheekpieces may suit.

runners_data.name: Gwen Tennyson
runners_data.note: Hold-up style badly suited to pace scenario, but showed improved speed last time and Connor Beasley takes over
runners_data.comment: Ordinary form in maiden/novice on the AW over 5f/6f and best watched for now
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't offer much on first two starts but showed speed and she improved when third, to one who now has a mark of 72, in C&D novice (50-1) 12 days ago; switches to a handicap at an appropriate level; possibilities.

runners_data.name: Saxon Grace
runners_data.note: Another hold-up horse facing tactical disadvantage, needs significant pace collapse to feature prominently
runners_data.comment: 0-9 but not without promise in March for new yard and has each-way possibilities
runners_data.spotlight: Heavily supported on stable debut (sixth) on Wolverhampton AW in March and was only headed deep inside the final furlong when fourth at Carlisle (6f, good; 11-2) a fortnight ago; this sharp 5f could prove ideal.

runners_data.name: Enjoy The Night
runners_data.note: 278 days off and hold-up style makes this a very tough assignment against this specific pace shape
runners_data.spotlight: Down the field in three novice/maiden events and it was a similar tale in added tongue-tie on handicap debut at Thirsk (5f; 28-1) last September; has left the Quinns since; hard to be interested in him back from an absence unless the market speaks favourably; has been gelded.

runners_data.name: Powernap
runners_data.note: Recent course runner-up with tongue-tie retained, but hold-up style fights against probable pace dynamics
runners_data.comment: Took a step back in the right direction latest; each-way player if backing that up.
runners_data.spotlight: 0-10; runner-up in added tongue-tie over C&D (Havin A Flyer fourth) 12 days ago; occupied that same position at Wetherby (about 5f, good to firm) subsequently; consistent but has had plenty of chances.

runners_data.name: Brain Freeze
runners_data.note: Recent Redcar winner racing prominently should suit this scenario, though Michael Dods 5lb claimer takes over
runners_data.comment: Her two best runs have come here but she is up in grade and out of the weights today
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark in a tight finish at Redcar (5f; good to firm; 12-1) latest; that form has taken a couple of hits (second and third soundly beaten since) and has more to do from this 3lb higher mark; the prospect of rain is also a legitimate concern.

runners_data.name: Sparkling Wine
runners_data.note: Uncontested leader will dictate fractions, improvement needed but tactical advantage is significant here
runners_data.comment: Modest form in two runs 387 days apart; minor handicaps beckon
runners_data.spotlight: Sent off at big prices all three starts; only seventh of eight (beaten over 12l) in a 6f fillies' novice at Ripon (33-1) under a month ago; improvement necessary, even at this lowly level, on handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Tanaka
runners_data.note: Struggling hold-up horse whose style is completely wrong for this race shape and pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on all four starts last term and needs to improve markedly; poor draw
runners_data.spotlight: Failed to beat a rival in two starts for Kevin Ryan, and has done little better since joining David O'Meara; it's tough to envisage her troubling Powernap or Havin A Flyer on recent C&D evidence; focus elsewhere.

races.paceDynamic: Sparkling Wine will set the pace from the front with no obvious challengers, creating an uncontested lead in this small field. Havin A Flyer and Brain Freeze may track her in second and third, but neither is aggressive enough to pressure the leader early. The remaining five runners - Gwen Tennyson, Saxon Grace, Enjoy The Night, Powernap and Tanaka - are all hold-up horses who will need to close from the back. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those who can track the pace, as the hold-up horses will struggle to peg back an uncontested leader over this minimum trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Sparkling Wine gets an easy lead and maintains her gallop...
scenarios.body: She'll dictate fractions and prove difficult to peg back over 5f. The prominent runners tracking her will have the best chance if she tires, but may lack the acceleration to catch her.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Havin A Flyer or Brain Freeze sit close enough to pounce...
scenarios.body: They can use their superior class to sweep past Sparkling Wine in the final furlong. Their prominent running style is perfectly suited to this pace scenario with multiple hold-up horses behind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Charges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and one closer finds gaps...
scenarios.body: Powernap or Gwen Tennyson could benefit from their recent good form despite the tactical disadvantage. However, five hold-up horses will struggle for room and pace bias makes this unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Sparkling Wine stops quickly and creates a slow pace...
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where the best horse on the day can win regardless of tactics. This would open the door for any of the classier hold-up horses to strike.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Sparkling Wine gets a soft lead through early fractions - she could prove very hard to peg back
Monitor if any of the prominent runners Havin A Flyer or Brain Freeze press Sparkling Wine early and create genuine pace
Check how quickly the hold-up brigade can get into contention turning for home with limited pace assistance
Watch for traffic problems among the five hold-up horses who will all need luck in running from the back
Observe if Powernap can reproduce recent course form despite the tactical disadvantage of her running style

races.name: Download The Raceday Ready App Handicap

runners_data.name: Equity Law
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with C&D form, should get an easy lead with David Allan's tactical nous, 11 days since last run keeps him sharp
runners_data.comment: Again travelled strongly when sixth here 15 days ago and remains in good form
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner off 1lb higher last September; two good runs when third at Ripon in April (5f, good) and at Thirsk (5f, good to firm) last month but he hasn't done as well since.

runners_data.name: Isle Of Lismore
runners_data.note: Prominent racer stepping back up in trip, Robert Cowell's 1 from 10 recent record is concerning, 21-day break
runners_data.comment: Returns from an absence but on a competitive mark and he's right at home on slow ground
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner in May 2021 (heavy); wasn't in top form last season so has dropped to a good mark but he was well beaten on soft at Haydock on reappearance.

runners_data.name: Le Beau Garcon
runners_data.note: Handy runner with strong course record, Joanna Mason takes over, 34 days off could leave her needing the run
runners_data.spotlight: Four wins, the latest on reappearance at Ayr last May (5f, good); fair fourth on last month's Ripon reappearance (5f, good), although that form hasn't worked out; good second to Equity Law here last September and, with his stable going well, he's worth considering.

runners_data.name: Arctic Summer
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with concerning finishing tendencies, tried cheekpieces at Carlisle just 2 days ago unsuccessfully
runners_data.comment: Ex-French (won over 6f at Chantilly in 2024); going suits; not in top form; headgear tried
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-French; won over 6f at Chantilly in 2024 (very soft); rather disappointing since joining present yard, including at Carlisle on Tuesday when tried in cheekpieces (retained).

runners_data.name: Winchurch
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse effective at this distance, Michael Appleby's 0 from 28 strike rate is worrying, 10 days between runs
runners_data.comment: Drawn to attack again and fine on Tapeta but an 8lb rise will test him into a deeper race
runners_data.spotlight: Effective at 5f/6f on turf and AW; easy winner at Nottingham in April (6f, good) for which he went back up 8lb; not so good on AW next time but has a chance back on turf.

runners_data.name: Glory Fighter
runners_data.note: Prominent veteran with two C&D wins, Paul Midgley in better form recently, 26-day gap since disappointing effort
runners_data.comment: Made all at Nottingham last month and not disgraced at Ripon; should make another bold bid
runners_data.spotlight: Two of 11 wins have been over C&D; latest success was at Nottingham (5f, good) in April but rather disappointing since; has a bit to prove.

runners_data.name: Lucius Aurelius
runners_data.note: Forward-going type with excellent course record, 5lb claimer reduces burden, 20 days since poor Haydock run
runners_data.comment: 17th time lucky when winning at Catterick last month; 5lb rise might find him out
runners_data.spotlight: Record here is 2231, his win coming over 5f in April (good); can be forgiven a below-par effort next time after being restless in stalls; interesting back here.

races.paceDynamic: Equity Law will set the early pace from his prominent position, with Isle Of Lismore, Le Beau Garcon, Glory Fighter and Lucius Aurelius all likely to race handily behind. The lack of a committed front-runner means the pace will be sustainable rather than frantic, allowing the prominent racers to maintain their positions without excessive early pressure. Arctic Summer and Winchurch will be held up from the rear but face the challenge of making up ground in a small field where the leaders can control proceedings. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track the pace and have the tactical speed to strike in the final furlong when the tempo lifts.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Equity Law sets a steady tempo without being harassed early
scenarios.body: The handy horses can travel comfortably before quickening, while the hold-up pair struggle to make inroads from the back in a slowly-run race. Prominent positioning proves decisive when the real running begins inside the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Success
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely strong with multiple prominent runners vying for position
scenarios.body: The increased tempo will set up the race for the hold-up horses to close from the rear. Winchurch's finishing kick becomes more potent when the leaders have been softened up by a searching gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Experience Tells
scenarios.trigger: If the small field and good ground favour the older campaigners with course knowledge
scenarios.body: Glory Fighter's two course wins and Equity Law's C&D success give them crucial advantages in a tactical affair. Their racecourse familiarity allows them to position perfectly for the decisive moment.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Equity Law fails to go forward or gets shuffled back early
scenarios.body: The lack of an established leader creates a stop-start tempo that turns the race into a sprint finish. Any horse with tactical speed and good positioning in the final quarter-mile can capitalise on the messy pace dynamics.

watchPoints.text: Arctic Summer's tendency to fade in the finish makes her vulnerable if the pace is anything other than strong early
Glory Fighter needs to bounce back from recent poor form despite his course advantages and tactical speed
Lucius Aurelius carries significant weight relief with the 5lb claimer but must overcome his poor recent Haydock effort
Le Beau Garcon's 34-day break could leave her short of peak fitness in a competitive sprint handicap
Winchurch's hold-up style faces a tactical challenge in a small field where the leaders can dictate terms

races.name: Try Racing TV For Free Now Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Sixpack
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with proven form at this trip, likely to dictate terms from the front with Jason Orr aboard
runners_data.comment: Stays 1m6f and he battled on best to win over 1m4f at Doncaster last month; up 3lb
runners_data.spotlight: Three good runs this season, notably when winning off 3lb lower over 1m4f at Doncaster early last month (good to firm); stays 1m6f well; not disgraced on good to soft last time and one with a chance.

runners_data.name: Robert Johnson
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning after 426 days off but has excellent course record with two wins here previously
runners_data.spotlight: Has won seven of his 23 races at up to 2m2f, including two over 1m4f here in 2023 and 2024; creditable 2l third of seven at Newbury on latest start in April 2025 when with Tracy Waggott; now 4lb lower and an interesting contender on stable debut despite 426-day absence.

runners_data.name: Lightning Tiger
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits if pace is honest, returning to scene of his only handicap win last October
runners_data.comment: Has won over this trip on turf; last month's Thirsk reappearance has been franked; hood on
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced; won over 1m4f here on handicap debut (soft) last October; fair form since and could go well, although he didn't run to his best on only previous try at this trip; hood on for second time.

runners_data.name: Baileys Khelstar
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good form this season, ideally positioned to track the early pace and challenge late
runners_data.comment: 1lb higher than for his last win, which came over this trip; this is easier than last time
runners_data.spotlight: Missed 2025 but proved he has retained his ability with two good runs this year, notably when second to an in-form stablemate of Sixpack over 2m at Newbury last time (good to firm); acts on any ground; can go well.

runners_data.name: Military Air
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse carrying top weight of 137lbs, needs strong gallop to show his Listed race class
runners_data.comment: Ex-French; well beaten on stable debut at Pontefract (1m2f) last month
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-French; winner at Lyon Parilly on his debut in 2024 (1m, very soft) and third in a Longchamp Listed race (1m4f, good to soft) last year; bit disappointing since 45,000gns purchase last autumn but capable of better than he has shown in Britain.

runners_data.name: Gibside
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with two course wins including this very race last year, though form has declined this season
runners_data.comment: On a good mark but needs to leave his four efforts this season a long way behind him
runners_data.spotlight: Two course wins, including this race off 8lb lower in 2024 (good to firm); highly tried and not been at his best this season but quite interesting down in grade.

races.paceDynamic: Sixpack will set the early tempo with Baileys Khelstar and Gibside sitting close, creating a moderate gallop in this small field. With only six runners, there's limited pace pressure early, allowing the front division to dictate terms through steady fractions. The lack of genuine speed horses means this becomes a tactical affair where positioning matters more than raw pace. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those with tactical speed who can track the pace and finish, disadvantaging pure hold-up horses who need a stronger gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Gallop Suits Trackers
scenarios.trigger: If Sixpack maintains honest fractions without being pressured early
scenarios.body: The moderate but consistent pace allows prominent runners to travel smoothly and finish strongly down the home straight. Baileys Khelstar and Gibside can track the leader perfectly while Lightning Tiger gets the right setup from his hold-up style.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Favours Class
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes very steady and the race turns into a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure creates a tactical affair where superior class and finishing kick become decisive factors. Military Air's Listed race experience and Robert Johnson's proven ability at this trip come to the fore in a slowly-run contest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If Sixpack gets an uncontested lead and the field settles too far back
scenarios.body: The patient ride allows Sixpack to control the race completely and kick clear when the pace lifts entering the straight. His recent Doncaster win shows he can dominate when getting his own way, while the hold-up horses struggle to make up ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If all runners sit and wait creating an extremely slow early pace
scenarios.body: The crawling fractions turn this into a pure speed contest over the final three furlongs where tactical position matters most. Gibside's course knowledge and Lightning Tiger's finishing kick become crucial in a bunched finish where the best turn of foot wins.

watchPoints.text: Robert Johnson returning after 426 days absence - fitness could be a major question mark despite his course record
Military Air carrying 137lbs top weight in small field - could struggle to concede weight if pace doesn't suit hold-up style
Lightning Tiger only has two runs on good going with zero wins - surface preference unclear despite course win on soft
Sixpack could get uncontested lead if Baileys Khelstar and Gibside don't press early - dangerous scenario for front runner
Baileys Khelstar missed entire 2025 season - watch for any ring rustiness despite two good runs since returning

races.name: Racing Again 22nd June Handicap

runners_data.name: Qazaq

runners_data.name: Tattie Bogle
runners_data.note: Recent winner with prominent style perfectly suited to tracking the lone front-runner, solid course form
runners_data.comment: Won for the first time on turf at Musselburgh in April; runner-up at Ayr 12 days ago.
runners_data.spotlight: Winner off a 2lb lower mark at Musselburgh in April (7f, good); two sound placed efforts on last two starts; solid run on only previous run here; chance.

runners_data.name: Uppercase

runners_data.comment: Promising start to career but his last two runs have seen his form dip; still low mileage
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced maiden; tends to pull hard but sound run when third at Yarmouth last time (7f, good); can make the running which would be an asset round here; interesting.

runners_data.name: In A Hurry
runners_data.note: Disappointing recent form undermines previous course promise, prominent style suits but needs significant improvement
runners_data.comment: Two handicap placings but she's been right out of form in her three starts since
runners_data.spotlight: Won a Thirsk maiden last June (7f, good); good third over this C&D next time (good to firm) but has been very disappointing on her last four starts (two of them this season) so has plenty to prove at present.

runners_data.name: Imperial Guard
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist faces wrong race shape, recent form over shorter distances suggests stamina questions
runners_data.comment: Yet to win for this trainer (0-11); readily outpaced on seasonal reappearance; visor on.
runners_data.spotlight: Only win was at Kempton in 2024 when with Andrew Balding; ran three sound races over 5f/6f for Michael Dods in May 2025; mainly disappointing since, including with cheekpieces (left off today) last time.

runners_data.name: Habrdi
runners_data.note: Two recent placings at Ayr show current form, but hold-up style needs pace collapse to be effective
runners_data.comment: Up-and-down profile but second over C&D recently and leading claims if backing that up
runners_data.spotlight: Only turf win was in a Brighton novice (6f, soft) for Jane Chapple-Hyam in October 2023; however, he has run two sound races to be placed at Ayr on last two starts (7f, good to firm); each-way chance.

runners_data.name: Jenni
runners_data.note: Poor recent form and absence since May raise serious questions despite previous course success
runners_data.comment: 7f winner last spring but slow starts have become a big issue; looks risky back at 6f
runners_data.spotlight: Musselburgh winner off 8lb higher in May last year (7f, good); below par both runs in 2026; needs to bounce back.

runners_data.name: Coconut Bay
runners_data.note: Course winner last year with ideal front-running style, recent return suggests retaining ability despite age
runners_data.comment: Most wins over 7f; disappointing at Catterick last time
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins last June/July including this race on good ground and another handicap over C&D on good to firm in July; creditable third at Ayr early last month but not so good since; makes a quick reappearance after a below-par run on soft ground on Monday (6f).

runners_data.name: Pouting
runners_data.note: Long absence since wind operation and maiden status make this ambitious return assignment very difficult
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Richard Hughes; bought for 14,000gns last July; 11-race maiden; tailed off on only start for this yard (second run after wind op) last August; off since; best watched for now.

races.paceDynamic: Coconut Bay is the sole confirmed front-runner and will set a controlled, sustainable gallop without early pressure. Vince Le Prince and Tattie Bogle will track prominently behind, while the large contingent of hold-up horses including Qazaq, Uppercase, and Habrdi will settle towards the rear. With limited early pace, the tempo will be modest through the middle stages before quickening late. This setup strongly favours prominent runners and front-runners who can control their own destiny rather than hold-up horses facing a tactical disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Coconut Bay Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Coconut Bay gets an uncontested lead and dictates fractions.
scenarios.body: The front-runner can control the race tactically and kick clear when ready, while prominent trackers get first run on any faltering pace-setter. Early pace control proves decisive in this tactical affair.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If Vince Le Prince or Tattie Bogle pressure Coconut Bay from the outset.
scenarios.body: The increased pace will stretch the field and expose the large hold-up contingent, but may also set things up for a closer with the strongest finishing kick. The prominent duo benefit from pressing forward early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint from the 2f pole.
scenarios.body: The numerous hold-up horses get their ideal scenario with a slow pace turning into a dash, allowing superior class and finishing speed to dominate. Qazaq and Uppercase particularly benefit from this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Coconut Bay goes too slow and multiple horses make simultaneous moves.
scenarios.body: A messy, stop-start affair develops where positioning becomes crucial and the race fragments into multiple groups. Any horse able to secure a clear run and maintain momentum benefits from the tactical confusion.

watchPoints.text: Coconut Bay setting too slow early fractions could completely change the race dynamic and favour hold-up horses
Vince Le Prince breaking aggressively from the gates to pressure the front-runner and force stronger pace
Uppercase pulling hard early and getting into speed battle that compromises stamina reserves for finish
Qazaq's positioning in the first two furlongs will indicate whether connections believe pace will be strong enough
Tattie Bogle tracking Coconut Bay closely suggests Johnston's confidence in current form and tactical approach
